page: Amazon Web Services i4g.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. The instance features the arm64 architecture driven by an AWS Graviton2 implementation utilizing 32 dedicated physical cores on ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 silicon clocked at 2.5 GHz. Each core runs a single thread with no simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is sized at 256.0 GB total RAM, offering 8.0 GB of memory per core. The server provides 7500 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and operates without discrete GPU acceleration. Baseline network throughput is rated at 19 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate solid mid-range performance across sustained multi-threaded workloads, backed by an uncached read memory bandwidth of 151.6 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 75.04 GB/sec. The instance scored 48581.53 on stress-ng multi-core and 11678.0 on Geekbench multi-core. In transactional tests, it delivered 20435.28 points in PassMark database operations and 36.96 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. However, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, with a Geekbench single-core score of 962.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 20.27 GB/sec, illustrating that per-core throughput is modest compared to x86 alternatives.

Cost efficiency is centered on high I/O throughput and balanced resource density. The Graviton2 processor and bundled 7.5 TB NVMe storage eliminate auxiliary block storage overhead while providing predictable single-threaded core execution. The configuration fits high-throughput transactional databases, distributed file systems, real-time analytics engines, and in-memory caches requiring dense local NVMe storage and stable memory bandwidth.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by a 32-core AWS Graviton2 ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro architecture, it allocates 32 dedicated physical cores with single-threading, 256.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core), and 7500 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, alongside 19 Gbps baseline networking. Without discrete GPUs, its performance profile favors sustained multi-threaded execution and I/O-intensive workloads, posting 48581.53 in stress-ng multi-core and 36.96 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread benchmarks like Geekbench single-core (962.0) are lower, its generous memory capacity and integrated NVMe flash offer strong qualitative hardware density. The instance is suitable for transactional databases, NoSQL clusters, search indexing, and real-time data streaming.
